function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run as a script) to finish the whole workflow.  
I’ve also included the exact file contents that will be created/updated so you can review them before committing.

> **NOTE** – I can’t actually run `git clone` or `git push` from here, but the commands below will do it for you on your machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
# 1. Clone the repo
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse & create/update files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

> *Assumption:* The repo contains a simple Node.js app that listens on port **3000** (common for Express apps).  
> If the actual port differs, change `EXPOSE 3000` and the CMD accordingly.

```dockerfile
# 2.1 Dockerfile
# Use a lightweight Node.js base image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> Save this as `Dockerfile` in the repo root (overwrites any existing one).

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

> *Assumption:* You’ll build/push an image named `nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> Replace `<YOUR_REGISTRY>` with your registry (e.g., `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`).

```yaml
# 2.2 k8s-deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_REGISTRY>/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> Save this as `k8s-deployment.yaml` in the repo root.

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow

> *Assumption:* You’ll push the image to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`).  
> Make sure you have a personal access token (PAT) with `write:packages` scope stored in the repo’s secrets as `GHCR_TOKEN`.

```yaml
# 2.3 .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GHCR_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> Create the directory `.github/workflows` if it doesn’t exist, then save the above as `docker-build.yml`.

---

## 3️⃣ Add all changed files to Git

```bash
# 3. Add all new/modified files
git add Dockerfile k8s-deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
# 4. Commit the changes
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# 4. Push to remote
git push origin main
```

---

### Quick sanity check

After pushing, you should see:

* A new **Actions** tab with a successful run that builds & pushes the image.
* The `Dockerfile`, `k8s-deployment.yaml`, and workflow file committed to the repo.

If you run into any errors (e.g., missing secrets, wrong image tags), adjust the placeholders accordingly. Happy coding!
